text:
maya: Heads up — the latest apples-to-apples runs with the replay harness are showing a ~12% tail regression for the 8k sequence case when we enable the new kernel picker. wondering if this is a KV-warmup artifact or a batching heuristic mismatch. anyone seen this pattern?

ton y: can you paste the run config + the seed traffic profile? is this on dedicated or local perf nodes?

maya: dedicated cluster (p3x8-type), test id `replay-2026-03-12/kv-warmup-check`. profile: QPS ramp to 600 -> 600 steady -> 3x 2s bursts at 1200. generator config snippet:
```
qps_ramp: {start: 20, target: 600, duration_s: 60}
burst_pattern: [{qps:1200, dur_s:2, repeat:3, spacing_s:30}]
kv_warmup: enabled
batching: {max_batch_tokens: 4096, latency_slo_ms: 120}
```

li: thanks. I looked at the perf trace — the regression lines up with a spike in `kv_lookup_ms` during the ramp tail. appears 18-25% of requests hit cache-miss behavior right after a burst and then latency climbs.

anika: hmm — is the kernel picker switching to the smaller-kernel codepath after the burst because the observed batch size distribution changes? sounds like the selector threshold might be too aggressive for long-tail traffic.

maya: that was my thought. profiler shows kernel selection flip at ~t+73s (right after the first burst). stack dump excerpt: 
```
select_kernel(model=redwood-7b, seq=8192, obs_batch=2) -> kernel_v2_small (fallback)
per-request: choose_by_estimated_throughput (est=320 tok/s)
```

tony: If kernel_v2_small has worse kv_hot-path support, that could explain higher lookup ms. Li — can you confirm KV hit-rate across the timeline?

li: KV hit-rate: overall 94% but dips to 78% for 30s after bursts. KV lookup latency distribution shift: median 1.8ms -> 5.5ms; 95p 3.4ms -> 12.1ms.

anika: That aligns. Two potential issues: (1) generator's burst spacing is evicting prefixes from the in-process KV cache due to our cache TTL heuristic, (2) kernel selector relies on short-term batch size histogram that's polluted by the burst tails.

maya: Proposed experiment: run 3 variants apples-to-apples — keep generator identical and flip only one variable per run: A) force kernel_v2_large, B) increase KV local TTL to 120s, C) smooth batching estimator (moving average window 20s). Compare 99p gen latency and token cost.

tony: yes. Also capture perf counters: `gpu_kernel_choice`, `kv_hit`, `batch_size_histogram` and include the raw request timestamps so we can compute inter-arrival autocorrelation.

li: I'll run the three variants on a fresh nodepool. quick note: for variant A we need a pinned model variant to avoid runtime auto-fallback; add `force_kernel=kernel_v2_large` to the runtime args.

infra-bot: deploy started: replay-2026-03-12/kv-experiments (A,B,C). 3 runs queued across 3 nodepools. ETA ~18m.

maya: thanks. follow-up ask — when we publish the apples-to-apples comparison, let's present per-epoch warmup behavior (first 120s) not just steady-state averages. those warmup shapes are the whole point here.

anika: agreed. also plot per-request kernel label over time (color-coded) so we can visibly correlate kernel flips with KV misses.

li: first run completed (A). preliminary: 99p latency improved by 9% vs baseline, KV hit-rate unchanged. kernel labels show no flip — pinned worked. raw: `99p=210ms -> 191ms`

tony: promising. if hit-rate unchanged that points at kernel implementation differences (hot path). can we get a flamegraph for the kernel hot path?

li: uploading short flame snippet: 
```
kernel_v2_large: cpu_copy_ms 0.6 -> 0.3, kv_lookup_ms 1.9 -> 1.2, attn_kernel_ms 12.4 -> 11.8
kernel_v2_small: cpu_copy_ms 0.5, kv_lookup_ms 5.4, attn_kernel_ms 11.6
```

maya: looks like kernel_v2_small has an inefficient KV-path (maybe mem layout causes scattered lookups).

anika: let's keep A as a mitigant for now and work on a long-term fix: (1) adjust selector's scoring to favor kernels with better kv_hot-path when kv_hit_rate < 95%, (2) refactor small-kernel kv access pattern.

li: running variant B now (KV TTL up). early: KV hit-rate holds at 92-96% after bursts, but 99p latency only improves 3%.

maya: sounds like TTL helps but doesn't fully address kernel inefficiency.

tony: run C next — smoothing selector window. if that avoids rapid flips we might get both stable kernel choice and improved tail without code changes.

infra-bot: run B completed, run C queued. ETA ~11m.

anika: FYI for the apples-to-apples doc: include generator params (burst spacing, ramp slope), node spec, and the exact runtime flags. reviewers will want to reproduce. also add a small guidance blurb: "avoid aggressive selector windows <10s for bursty long-tail workloads" based on these results.

maya: agreed. final ask: Li, after C finishes can you snapshot the `batch_size_histogram` and `kernel_choice_timeline` and paste into the thread? we'll collate into a short perf blurb for eng-runtime.

li: will do. C started.

(threads to continue with results...)
